82:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Infitar Al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Qudamah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Mu'adh stood up and prayed the late 'Isha' prayer, and he prolonged it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you tempted, O Mu'adh? Where were you when it came to 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High', 'By the forenoon', and 'When the sky is split asunder'? The original hadith is found in the two Sahihs, but the mention of When the sky is split asunder is mentioned in the separate surahs of Al-Nasa'i. It was mentioned earlier in the narration of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever would like to see the Day of Resurrection with his own eyes, let him recite: 'When the sun is wrapped up', 'When the sky is split asunder', and 'When the sky is split asunder'." In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says: When the heaven is cleft asunder, meaning, it is split, as God the Almighty says: The heaven will be split asunder by it, “And when the stars are scattered,” meaning, they fall, And when the seas gush forth, Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God will cause some of them to gush forth into others. Al-Hasan said: God will cause some of them to gush forth into others, and their water will disappear. Qatada said: Its fresh water will mix with its salt water. Al-Kalbi said: It will be filled. And when the graves are scattered, Ibn Abbas said: It will be searched. Al-Suddi said: It will be scattered means it will move and whoever is in it will emerge. A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind, meaning if this happens, this will happen. And the Almighty’s statement: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? This is a threat, not as some people imagine, that it is a guide to the answer where He said, The Generous, so that their speaker might say, His generosity has deceived him. Rather, the meaning of this verse is: What has deceived you, O son of Adam, concerning your Generous, meaning the Great, Lord, so that you committed a sin and met Him with an inappropriate behavior? As it came in the hadith, God the Almighty will say on the Day of Resurrection, O son of Adam, what has deceived you concerning Me? O son of Adam, what did you answer the messengers? Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us that Omar heard a man reciting, O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Omar said, Ignorance. He also said: Omar bin Shaibah told us, Abu Khalaf told us, Yahya Al-Bakka told us, I heard Ibn Omar say, and he recited this verse, O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Ibn Omar said, By God, his ignorance deceived him. He said, “It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Al-Rabi bin Khathim, and Al-Hasan something similar. Qatada said, ‘What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?’ Nothing has deceived the son of Adam except this enemy, Satan.” Al-Fudayl bin Iyad said, If he were to say to me, ‘What has deceived you concerning me?’ I would say, ‘Your curtain is lowered.’ Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said, If he were to say to me, ‘What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?’ I would say, ‘The generosity of the Generous has deceived me.’ Al-Baghawi said: Some of the scholars of allusion said: He only said By your Generous Lord without the rest of His names and attributes, as if He taught him the answer. What this speaker imagined is not in vain, because he only mentioned His Generous Name to point out that one should not respond to the Generous with ugly deeds and immoral actions. Al-Baghawi narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi and Muqatil that they said: This verse was revealed about Al-Aswad bin Shuraik who struck the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was not punished in the current situation, so God Almighty revealed: What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? And the saying of God the Almighty: {Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you} meaning, what has deceived you concerning the Generous Lord? {Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you} meaning, He made you sound, upright, of moderate stature, erect in the best of forms and shapes. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Jarir told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah told me, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Bishr ibn Jahash al-Qurashi, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) spat one day into his hand, then placed his finger on it and said: God the Almighty said: O son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from something like this? Then, when I proportioned you and proportioned you, you walked between two cool places, and the earth was slow from you. You gathered and withheld until, when you reached the collarbones, I said, Should I give charity? But when is the time for charity? Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Jarir ibn Uthman. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, and Yahya bin Hamza followed him, on the authority of Thawr bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Maysarah. God the Almighty said: In whatever form He wills, He has put you together. Mujahid said: In whatever resemblance a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, Mutahhar ibn al-Haytham told us, Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What will be born to you? He said: O Messenger of God, what is the possibility that a child will be born to me? Either a boy or a girl. He said: Then who will he resemble? He said: O Messenger of God, who will he resemble? Either his father or his mother? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) then said: “No, do not say that. When the sperm settles in the womb, God the Almighty brings to it every lineage between it and Adam.” Have you not read this verse in the Book of God the Almighty: In whatever form He wills, He put you together. He said: Your appearance. Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Mutahhar ibn Al-Haytham. God the Almighty says: No! Rather, you deny the Judgment. That is, what drives you to confront the Generous One and confront Him with sins is a denial in your hearts of the Resurrection, reward, and judgment. God the Almighty says: And indeed, over you are guardians, * Noble and recording * Who know whatever you do. Meaning, there are noble and recording angels over you, so do not confront them with shameful deeds, for they record all your deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Wakee' told us, Sufyan and Musa'ar told us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Honor the noble recording angels who do not leave you except in one of two situations: major ritual impurity janabah and defecation. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it and connected it with another wording, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Karamah told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God forbids you from exposing yourself to the nakedness, so be shy before the angels of God who are with you, the honorable recorders who do not leave you except in three situations: defecation, major ritual impurity, and ritual bathing. So if one of you performs ritual bathing in the open, let him cover himself with his garment, a wall covering, or his camel.” Then Hafs ibn Sulayman said: The hadith is weak, but it has been narrated from him and his hadith is possible. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ziyad ibn Ayoub told us, Mubashar ibn Ismail al-Halabi told us, Tamam ibn Nujayh told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, meaning al-Basri, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are no two memorizers who raise to God, the Almighty, what they have memorized in one day, and he sees at the beginning of the scroll and at the end of it a request for forgiveness, except that God, the Almighty, says: I have forgiven My servant what is between the two ends of the scroll.” Then he said: It is unique. Narrated by Tamam bin Nujayh, who is trustworthy in hadith. I said: Ibn Ma’in authenticated him, but Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn ‘Adi declared him weak. Ibn Hibban accused him of fabricating hadiths. Imam Ahmad said, I do not know the truth about his story. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said, “Ishaq bin Sulayman Al-Baghdadi, known as Al-Qalusi, told us, Bayan bin Hamran told us, Salam told us, from Mansur bin Zadhan, from Muhammad bin Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said, ‘The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “God has angels who know the children of Adam—and I think he said, and they know their deeds—so when they look at a slave who does an act of obedience to God, they mention him among themselves and name him and say, ‘So-and-so succeeded tonight, so-and-so was saved tonight.’ But when they look at a slave who does an act of disobedience to God, they mention him among themselves and name him and say, ‘So-and-so was doomed tonight.’” Then Al-Bazzar said, This Salam, I think he is Salam Al-Madaini, and he has weak hadith.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Jarir told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah told me, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Bishr ibn Jahash al-Qurashi, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) spat one day into his hand, then placed his finger on it and said: God the Almighty said: O son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from something like this? Then, when I proportioned you and proportioned you, you walked between two cool places, and the earth was slow from you. You gathered and withheld until, when you reached the collarbones, I said, Should I give charity? But when is the time for charity? Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Jarir ibn Uthman. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, and Yahya bin Hamza followed him, on the authority of Thawr bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Maysarah. God the Almighty said: In whatever form He wills, He has put you together. Mujahid said: In whatever resemblance a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, Mutahhar ibn al-Haytham told us, Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What will be born to you? He said: O Messenger of God, what is the possibility that a child will be born to me? Either a boy or a girl. He said: Then who will he resemble? He said: O Messenger of God, who will he resemble? Either his father or his mother? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) then said: “No, do not say that. When the sperm settles in the womb, God the Almighty brings to it every lineage between it and Adam.” Have you not read this verse in the Book of God the Almighty: In whatever form He wills, He put you together. He said: Your appearance. Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Mutahhar ibn Al-Haytham. If this hadith was authentic, it would have been decisive in this verse, but its chain of transmission is not proven, because Abu Saeed ibn Yunus said about Mutahhar ibn Al-Haytham that his hadith was abandoned. Ibn Hibban said, He narrates from Musa ibn Ali and others what does not resemble the hadith of reliable narrators. However, in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “A man said, ‘O Messenger of God, my wife has given birth to a black boy.’ He said, ‘Do you have camels?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘What are their colors?’ He said, ‘Red.’ He said, ‘Is there one with gray hair among them?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘How did that happen?’ He said, ‘Perhaps it is a matter of inheritance.’ He said, ‘Perhaps this is a matter of inheritance.’” Ikrimah said about God’s statement, In whatever form He wills, He has assembled you, meaning, “If... Qatada said: “In whatever form He willed, He put you together.” He said: God, our Lord, is able to do that. The meaning of this statement, according to these people, is that God Almighty is able to create the sperm in the ugly form of animals with strange creation, but with His power, kindness, and forbearance, He creates it in a good, upright, balanced, perfect form, with a good appearance and form. God the Almighty says: No! Rather, you deny the Judgment. That is, what drives you to confront the Generous One and confront Him with sins is a denial in your hearts of the Resurrection, reward, and judgment. God the Almighty says: And indeed, over you are guardians, * Noble and recording * Who know whatever you do. Meaning, there are noble and recording angels over you, so do not confront them with shameful deeds, for they record all your deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Wakee' told us, Sufyan and Musa'ar told us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Honor the noble recording angels who do not leave you except in one of two situations: major ritual impurity janabah and defecation. So when one of you performs ghusl, let him conceal himself behind a sacred wall, or behind his camel, or let his brother conceal himself." Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it and connected it with another wording, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Karamah told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God forbids you from exposing yourself to the nakedness, so be shy before the angels of God who are with you, the honorable recorders who do not leave you except in three situations: defecation, major ritual impurity, and ritual bathing. So if one of you performs ritual bathing in the open, let him cover himself with his garment, a wall covering, or his camel.” Then Hafs ibn Sulayman said: The hadith is weak, but it has been narrated from him and his hadith is possible. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ziyad ibn Ayoub told us, Mubashar ibn Ismail al-Halabi told us, Tamam ibn Nujayh told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, meaning al-Basri, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are no two memorizers who raise to God, the Almighty, what they have memorized in one day, and he sees at the beginning of the scroll and at the end of it a request for forgiveness, except that God, the Almighty, says: I have forgiven My servant what is between the two ends of the scroll.” Then he said: It is unique. Narrated by Tamam bin Nujayh, who is trustworthy in hadith. I said: Ibn Ma’in authenticated him, but Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn ‘Adi declared him weak. Ibn Hibban accused him of fabricating hadiths. Imam Ahmad said, I do not know the truth about his story. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said, “Ishaq bin Sulayman Al-Baghdadi, known as Al-Qalusi, told us, Bayan bin Hamran told us, Salam told us, from Mansur bin Zadhan, from Muhammad bin Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said, ‘The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “God has angels who know the children of Adam—and I think he said, and they know their deeds—so when they look at a slave who does an act of obedience to God, they mention him among themselves and name him and say, ‘So-and-so succeeded tonight, so-and-so was saved tonight.’ But when they look at a slave who does an act of disobedience to God, they mention him among themselves and name him and say, ‘So-and-so was doomed tonight.’” Then Al-Bazzar said, This Salam, I think he is Salam Al-Madaini, and he has weak hadith.
82:13: God Almighty tells us about the bliss that the righteous will attain, and they are those who obeyed God Almighty and did not meet Him with sins. Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Musa bin Muhammad on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar on the authority of Isa bin Yunus bin Abi Ishaq on the authority of Ubaid God on the authority of Muharib on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God only called them the righteous because they were righteous to their fathers and sons. Then he mentioned what the wicked will attain of Hell and eternal torment. For this reason, he said: They will enter it on the Day of Judgment, meaning the Day of Reckoning, Recompense, and Resurrection. And they will not be absent from it, meaning they will not be absent from the torment for a single hour, nor will their torment be lightened, nor will they be answered in what they ask of death or rest, even for one day. God Almighty’s statement: And what will make you know what is the Day of Judgment? is a glorification of the importance of the Day of Judgment. Then He confirmed it with His statement: Then what will make you know what is the Day of Judgment? Then He explained it by saying: The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, meaning no one will be able to… No one can benefit from it or be saved from it unless God gives permission to whomever He wills and is pleased with. We mention here the hadith, “O Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. I have no power over anything for you against God.” It was mentioned at the end of the interpretation of Surat Ash-Shu’ara’. For this reason, He said, And the Command that Day belongs to God, just as He said, Whose is the dominion today? To God, the One, the Prevailing. And as He said, The dominion that Day will belong to the Most Merciful. And as He said, Owner of the Day of Judgment. Qatada said, The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the Command that Day belongs to God. And the Command, by God, today belongs to God, but no one will dispute it with Him on that day. The end of the interpretation of Surat Al-Infitar. Praise and gratitude are due to God, and with Him is success and protection.
